title: When people think about Judas, they think about betrayal.
paragraphs: When people think about Judas, they think about betrayal.

Thirty pieces of silver.
A kiss in the garden.
A disciple handing over the Son of God.
But betrayal didn’t start in the garden.
It started much earlier.
Judas spent years walking beside Jesus.
He heard every sermon.
He watched storms obey a voice.
He saw demons flee, the blind receive sight, and the dead rise.
Yet proximity to Jesus is not the same as surrender to Jesus.
And that is where the real danger lived.
The Bible quietly reveals something about Judas many people overlook.
He managed the money bag… and sometimes took from it.
What began as a hidden compromise slowly shaped his heart.
Because the greatest spiritual collapses rarely begin with dramatic rebellion.
They begin with small distances.
A neglected conviction.
A private compromise.
A heart that slowly stops listening.
And over time, distance makes things possible that once felt unthinkable.
One of the most sobering realities in Scripture is this:
Judas was close enough to Jesus to hear His heartbeat at the table…
but far enough in his heart to sell Him for silver.

"Temptation rarely begins with betrayal.
It begins with distance."

"You can stand in the presence of Jesus
and still allow your heart to drift away."

"Some people leave God suddenly.
Most drift slowly."
This story is not only about Judas.
It is a warning to every believer who learns how to stay around the things of God without guarding the condition of their heart.

Because the most dangerous place spiritually
is not far from Jesus.
It is near Him… while slowly drifting away.
Do you think spiritual failure usually happens suddenly, or does it begin with small compromises over time?
